findings.concern: expandOccurrences(rule, {from, to}) cannot actually satisfy AC-9's own text ('Given any rule, when expandOccurrences(rule, {from, to}) is called, then it returns every occurrence date in [from, to]...') for any rule with anchorMode: 'completion'. Both of expandOccurrences's while-loops call nextOccurrence(rule, {after: current}) without ever supplying completedOn; nextOccurrence's completion branch (line ~287) throws TypeError whenever completedOn is undefined. Hand-verified: for any window that contains the rule's first occurrence (the common case), the second loop pushes that occurrence and then immediately calls nextOccurrence to check the next candidate, which throws before the loop can terminate normally — the function only returns without throwing when the window is empty and entirely before dtstart. Nothing in the type system, the docstring, or the plan scopes expandOccurrences to calendar-anchored rules only, and AC-9's literal 'any rule' wording is unqualified. This may be a defensible design consequence (a completion-anchored series' future occurrences are not enumerable without knowing future completion dates, so throwing may be the only honest answer), but as written it is an unflagged, silent gap between the AC's literal promise and the code's actual behavior for a rule shape the type system permits.

stepOnePeriodFromCompletion's docstring claims it 'computes exactly one period forward from completedOn, treating completedOn as the anchor for that step' — but for monthly/weekly/yearly completion-anchored rules whose byMonthday/byWeekday target has not yet occurred within completedOn's own period, findNextMonthlyOrYearly's candidateForPeriod(0) already exceeds completedOn and is returned without incrementing period, i.e. strictly less than one full period forward. Hand-verified: rule {freq:'monthly', byMonthday:25, anchorMode:'completion', interval:1}, nextOccurrence(rule, {after: any, completedOn: '2026-09-10'}) returns '2026-09-25' — 15 days later, not one month later. AC-7 only pins the daily/interval-3 case, where this always coincides with a true one-interval step; the PRD's own Technical Risks table already flags weekly/monthly/yearly completion-anchor behavior beyond AC-7 as untested and deferred (Likelihood L, Impact L), so the resulting behavior itself is a defensible, principled interpretation (reusing the exact same stepping functions rather than special-casing), not necessarily a bug — but the docstring's unconditional 'exactly one period forward' phrasing is inaccurate for these cases and should either be corrected or scoped to the daily case it is actually proven for.
